messages:
anya: Heads-up — onboarding Melusine-13B (v2 int4) hit a weird memory fragmentation pattern during canary. intermittent OOMs on dedicated nodes when load increases > ~30 qps.

devon: saw that. reproduction steps?

anya: can reproduce locally on a single GPU with the canary harness. steps: `./run_bench --model melusine13b-int4 --scenario summarization --concurrency 12 --batching-policy windowed --max_new_tokens 256` then after ~90s the process OOMs.

sam: stack? logs?

anya: paste from the agent: ```
E0331 14:12:05 kernel.cpp:452] AllocFailed: cudaMalloc failed (out of memory) while reserving KV cache for seq_len=1536
[...]
E0331 14:12:06 memmgr.cpp:218] fragmentation: free_chunks=42 largest_free=6.7GiB total_free=18.1GiB
```

lucy: fragmentation numbers suggest lots of small free chunks + one large chunk but allocator can't satisfy contiguous slab for prefetched tensors. happens more when `max_new_tokens` default is 256.

devon: interesting. did you try lowering `max_new_tokens` to 128?

anya: yes — with `max_new_tokens=128` the OOM disappears in the same run. throughput drops ~6% but stable.

qa-bot: quick eval results: summarization ROUGE-L before quant (float16) = 35.2, after int4 conversion (current canary) = 33.1. quality delta = -2.1 absolute.

sam: so two issues: mem frag + quality regression post-quant. are they related?

anya: maybe. our current quant pipeline uses per-channel symmetric 4-bit with outlier clipping. suspected clipped outliers affecting generation for long-tail prompts (summaries). but mem frag is triggered by request windows where some requests use 1536 token context + long gen.

lucy: propose triage plan: 1) lower default `max_new_tokens` for melusine canary to 128 in rollout config; 2) enable slot_compactor=on in the runtime for this model to reduce fragmentation; 3) run a targeted quality sweep (1000 summarization prompts) comparing int4 with float16 and int8 fallback.

devon: +1. also try `kv_prefetch=false` as a quick guard — prefetch causes larger contiguous allocations.

anya: tried `kv_prefetch=false` and OOMs also stopped but latency p99 increased ~12% under peak. tradeoff chart attached to PR.

sam: we should add automatic fallback policy: if canary sees >1 OOM in 5m, fallback to int8 variant (melusine13b-int8) and alert SRE. simple policy in routing layer.

lucy: agreed. Also add quality gating on rollout: if ROUGE-L delta <= -1.0 then hold rollout. That would catch the -2.1 regression.

devon: commands I used to reproduce: ```bash
# reproduce harness
git checkout bringup/melusine-int4
./tools/canary_harness --model melusine13b-int4 --qps 35 --concurrency 12 --max_new_tokens 256 --batch_window_ms 40
```

anya: here's a minimal runtime patch that helped on my machine: ```json
{"model":"melusine13b-int4","defaults":{"max_new_tokens":128,"slot_compactor":true,"kv_prefetch":false,"batch_window_ms":35}}
```

sam: can you open a PR with the config change + canary gating? we'll run the QA sweep on the cluster.

anya: opened PR #4523 with config and a small note. also added benchmark artifacts: p50/p95/p99 and memory maps.

qa-bot: QA sweep kickoff: comparing three variants: float16 (baseline), int4 (current), int8 (fallback). 1000 prompts, summarization set. ETA ~45m.

lucy: if QA shows quality drop persists on int4, we should consider redoing quant with outlier-aware symmetric per-channel + per-head bias correction (experimenting with 5-bit mapping also).

devon: pinging @infra for any kernel-level tricks — maybe we can enable lazy-kernel-load so big kernels aren't resident until needed.

infra-bot: noted. opened task INF-2701 to investigate allocator tuning and lazy kernel loads for the melusine family. assigned to @mike.

anya: status update after applying defaults patch and gating in canary: 0 OOMs in 2h of 40 qps spike. int4 quality still showing ROUGE-L 33.0 vs baseline 35.2. int8 variant ROUGE-L = 35.0 (close to baseline).

sam: OK looks like fallback to int8 keeps quality and avoids most cost savings but is safe. next steps: 1) keep int4 disabled for production until quant pipeline improved; 2) ship defaults (max_new_tokens=128, slot_compactor on, kv_prefetch off) to reduce frag risk; 3) continue quant experiments (per-channel outlier aware + 5-bit).

anya: I'll file a follow-up with quant experiment logs and a small eval harness comparing 4-bit schemes.

devon: thanks. one more thing — add a slow-start on canary traffic (10% -> 30% -> 100% over 24h) to reduce likelihood of hitting fragmentation cliffs during rollout.

lucy: noted. thanks all. :thumbsup:
